answer: New identities are not planted in open ground: each is grafted onto an existing node of a public trellis, and the weight it adds flows down to its sponsor instead of standing alone. A sponsor can bear only so much load, so a farm of k clones must find k load-bearing points, and every graft shows on the lattice. Auditors prune any branch whose nodes carry only their own descendants, and the grove keeps a record of which root each strand came from. Honest growth looks like a broad trellis; a farm looks like a sable brush of parallel lines from one root.
